claims.claim: The only explicit market-index item in the window is a mid-window note that the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed at record levels, which describes calm, rising markets rather than a shock.

Corporate news in the window is limited to a single large domestic merger announcement (Charter Communications and Time Warner Cable, $55.1 billion) and a report that Mediobanca intends to sell a 1.6% stake in Telecom Italia, neither of which is a systemic event.
The macroeconomic data point in the window is UK inflation turning negative at -0.1%, described as the first negative reading in many years.
A MERS outbreak in South Korea escalates across the window, from a third confirmed case to twelve cases by the final day.

Geopolitical items are numerous but locally contained: ISIS capture of Ramadi and displacement of tens of thousands, mosque bombings in Saudi Arabia, a bus attack in Balochistan, and calls by France and Germany for Russia to implement Minsk measures.

The most prominent institutional story of the window is the detention of six FIFA officials in Switzerland for extradition to the United States and the opening of Swiss criminal proceedings over World Cup awards, which has no direct financial-market channel.

The final day contains no financial or macroeconomic event of scale: a presidential inauguration in Nigeria, a volcanic eruption and evacuation in Japan, a surveillance-flight agreement, a car bomb, and a criminal sentencing.

competing_explanation: The least-weak candidate is the escalating MERS outbreak in South Korea, which quadruples in reported cases over the second half of the window and could in principle feed regional risk pricing; a second, weaker candidate is the UK's first negative inflation print in years, which touches rate expectations. Neither is of a scale that would normally register as a regime change, and neither clusters on or near the flagged day.
insufficient_evidence_reason: The window is dominated by natural disasters, regional armed conflict, sports, criminal justice and referendum results, none of which carries an obvious transmission channel into broad market volatility. The only clearly financial items are a single large sector merger, a small stake sale, and a note that US equity indices set record highs mid-window, which signals continuity rather than disruption. Nothing on or immediately before the flagged day is of macro or systemic significance, so the flag is more consistent with noise, or with a driver not captured in these items, than with any event described here.
